messages.author: a225fe7bebd5f312
messages.subject: Re: "Doubly Latent Models"
parts:
Hi Michael,

That's an important paper.  The answer is "mostly"--lavaan doesn't provide random slopes yet, but it's listed on the development page as a target or goal for the .06 series.  

Below is lavaan code for estimating Marsh et al.'s Model 4 using data from the Mplus website (example 9.11).  You can sub in the variables from 9.11 into the Mplus code in the Marsh et al. appendix to check.  Hopefully, this will get you started.  

mp9.11.dat <- read.table("https://www.statmodel.com/usersguide/chap9/ex9.11.dat",
                        header = F)
names(mp9.11.dat) <- c( "y1", "y2", "y3", "y4", "y5", "y6", "g", "clus")

head(mp9.11.dat)

model4 <- '

level: 1
wf1 =~ a*y1 + b*y2 + c*y3
wf2 =~ d*y4 + e*y5 + f*y6

wf1 ~ b.within*wf2

level: 2
bf1 =~ a*y1 + b*y2 + c*y3
bf2 =~ d*y4 + e*y5 + f*y6
bf1 ~ b.between*bf2


bflpe := b.between-b.within

'
library(lavaan)
model4.out <- cfa(model4, data=mp9.11.dat, cluster="clus")

summary(model4.out)

Best,

Joe

messages.author: a225fe7bebd5f312
messages.subject: Re: "Doubly Latent Models"
parts:
Here's the Mplus version (via MplusAutomation) for fun...

model4.mp <- mplusObject (
  TITLE = "Doubly-latent from Marsh, Model 4",
  VARIABLE = "CLUSTER is clus;",
  ANALYSIS = "TYPE = TWOLEVEL RANDOM;
  ESTIMATOR = ML;",
  
  MODEL = "%WITHIN% 
  wf1 by y1 (a);
  wf1 by y2 (b);
  wf1 by y3 (c);
  wf2 by y4 (d);
  wf2 by y5 (e);
  wf2 by y6 (f);
  wf1 ON wf2 (b_within);
  
  %BETWEEN% 
  bf1 by y1 (a);
  bf1 by y2 (b);
  bf1 by y3 (c);
  bf2 by y4 (d);
  bf2 by y5 (e);
  bf2 by y6 (f);
  bf1 ON bf2 (b_betwn);",
  
  MODELCONSTRAINT = "
  new(bflpe);
  bflpe = b_betwn - b_within;",
  rdata = mp9.11.dat)

model4.mp.out <- mplusModeler(model4.mp, "mp9.11.dat", modelout = "model4.mp.inp", run = 10L)

model4.mp.out$results$model$parameters
model4.mp.out$results$model$summaries
